root_motivation: A tenant can drop a table that a published tool, a chain, a stored chart, and a live handle all read, and nothing warns them -- host.table.drop drops the table and every row and knows nothing about consumers. ai-stack's LineageGraph (BTreeMap of nodes plus upstream/downstream adjacency), fixed effect table keyed by change kind and consumer kind, and breadth-first ranking weighted by observed use already answers this for ai-stack's own metrics/dashboard node kinds; this PRD ports the effect table, the ranking, and the report types, rewrites the node kinds for mcphost's own entities, persists the graph per tenant in SQLite, feeds usage counts from the runs ledger, and puts a gate in front of host.table.drop.
user_persona: A tenant maintaining tables that its own tools, chains, charts, and handles depend on; an agent about to drop or reshape a table and wants to see what breaks, and how badly, before it does.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a published python tool whose source calls mcphost.table.query("SELECT * FROM orders"), When lineage is read, Then an edge table:orders -> tool:<name> exists with evidence source_scan.
Given a table with no consumers, When host.table.drop is called without confirm, Then it drops as before and no refusal is written.

Given a chain whose step tool reads orders and 40 finished runs of that chain, When host.lineage.blast_radius("table:orders", "drop") is called, Then the chain appears with severity breaking, action from the effect table, and uses 40, ranked above a tool with 3 uses.

Given that table, When host.table.drop("orders") is called without confirm, Then lineage_blocked lists the chain and the tool with their uses and the table still exists; When called with confirm: true, Then the table is dropped, its nodes and edges are removed, and dependent chart and handle nodes are marked orphaned.
Given the effect table, When every (ChangeKind, consumer_kind) pair is evaluated in a test, Then each returns a defined effect, severity, and action, and Add is none for every consumer.
Given a stored chart and a live handle both derived from expenses, When host.lineage.trace("table:expenses") is called, Then both appear downstream with their kinds.
Given 150 downstream consumers, When trace is called, Then a handle returns with downstream_count 150 and trace_page returns them 50 at a time.
Given two tenants with a table of the same name, When tenant A reads blast radius, Then no node from tenant B appears.
Given a model_set role change on a column a chart uses, When applied, Then the response includes a degrading note naming the chart and the change is applied.
Given 1,000 nodes and 3,000 edges, When blast radius runs, Then it completes under 50 ms on the builder.
Given a python tool, When it calls mcphost.lineage.trace("table:orders"), Then it receives the same object the tool returns.

scope: src/lineage/graph.rs: LineageGraph, NodeKind {table, column, tool, chain, document, chart, handle, run}, ChangeKind {Drop, Rename, TypeChange, Remove, Add}, LineageNode, ImpactedNode, ImpactReport, TraceEntry, blast_radius, trace -- ported from ai-stack @ 4ef6c22 with node kinds rewritten for mcphost's own entities.
src/lineage/effects.rs: the effect table (effect_for(change_kind, consumer_kind) -> (effect, severity, action)), data in one match, exhaustive over every (ChangeKind, NodeKind) pair.

src/lineage/scan.rs: source scanning for a python tool's mcphost.table.{query,chart,handle}("...") calls, reusing sqlparser (already a dependency) to read table names out of the literal SQL rather than hand-rolling a second grammar.

src/lineage/mod.rs: persistence (30s per-tenant cache, invalidated on any edge write), register_edge/register_tool_publish/register_chain_publish, breaking_drop_consumers/cascade_table_drop (the drop gate's own entry points), change_notes (model_set's entry point), record_run_finished (the runs-ledger usage hook), and the three host.lineage.* tool handlers (blast_radius/trace/trace_page).

migrations/0057_lineage.sql + src/db.rs: lineage_nodes/lineage_edges tables and their Db methods (lineage_upsert_node/lineage_insert_edge/lineage_load_nodes/lineage_load_edges/lineage_bump_uses/lineage_delete_node_and_edges/lineage_mark_orphaned).
src/handler.rs: host.lineage.blast_radius/trace/trace_page tool descriptors and dispatch; host.table.drop gains an optional confirm argument.

src/tables.rs: table_drop's gate -- computes breaking_drop_consumers before the transaction, refuses lineage_blocked without confirm, writes a tenant_audit line on refusal or a confirmed override, cascades lineage cleanup after a successful drop.
src/tables_model.rs: model_set's role-key change now reports (never blocks on) degrading+ consumers via change_notes.
src/control.rs: tool_publish registers lineage edges after a successful publish (source-scan + declared reads for python/wasm, each chain step's own tool for a chain).

src/runs.rs: run_one_job bumps uses/last_used_unix on the finished run's own tool/chain node and transitively on every table upstream of it, once finalize_run confirms this call actually finalized the row.

src/kinds/mod.rs + src/kinds/python.rs + src/handler.rs (TenantLineageBridge) + src/runs.rs: CallCtx gains a lineage backend (LineageBackend/NoLineage), PY_RUNNER_SCRIPT's mcphost.lineage.trace/blast_radius call through to the exact host.lineage.* logic (AC12, P1 requirement 10).

Chart and handle are net-new node kinds with no existing mcphost feature owning their creation (mcphost has no chart-store or live-handle product yet) -- AC6/AC7/AC9 register them directly through the lineage module's own pub API (lineage::register_edge), the same integration point a future chart-store/live-handle PRD's own publish path would call.
non_goals: Column-level lineage inside SQL expressions -- edges are table and column references only (scan.rs reads FROM/JOIN table identifiers, never which columns a query selects).

Cross-tenant edges or sign-off from other tenants -- ai-stack's change_gate 'foreign domain' RequiresSignoff concept has no mcphost analogue; every graph load/write is strictly tenant_id-scoped (AC8).
The defensibility dossier, as-of reconstruction, legal hold, and ROI modules from ai-stack -- not ported.
Renaming tables -- mcphost has no rename tool; ChangeKind::Rename is defined (AC5 needs a full effect-table row for it) but nothing in this build calls it.

A real chart-store or live-handle product feature -- AC6/AC7/AC9's chart/handle nodes are registered directly via the lineage module's Rust API in tests, not through a new host.chart.*/host.handle.* tool surface (none is in this PRD's Engineering target).

Table -> column edges from a table's declared schema (requirement 4's last sentence) -- no AC exercises this, so it isn't wired; NodeKind::Column exists in the type system (AC5 needs it) but nothing currently creates a column node.
A host.document.* store and its derived_from edge trigger (requirement 4) -- no AC exercises it and no document-store product exists in mcphost yet.

additional.test_file_names_use_test_prefix_lineage: test_prefix lineage (the PRD's own frontmatter field): tests/lineage_ac<NN>_<slug>.rs, same convention as every other test file in this repo.
additional.version_bump_minor: PRD frontmatter build_version_bump: minor -- Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock/CHANGELOG.md bumped 0.63.0 -> 0.64.0 (renumbered during rebase: mcphost-chart-in-a-minute claimed 0.63.0 first, landing on main ahead of this branch).
additional.ac11_deferred_operator_provisioned: AC11 is a Live acceptance criterion (a fresh tenant against a deployed box, receipt under docs/receipts/) -- deferred, not built or tested here; a build agent never provisions or deploys infrastructure.
additional.drop_gate_blocks_on_breaking_only: Open question default taken: host.table.drop blocks only on severity breaking, never on degrading regardless of use count -- the PRD's own stated default, no override implemented.
additional.orphaned_nodes_kept_not_deleted: Open question default taken: a confirmed drop's dependent chart/handle nodes are flagged orphaned: true and kept, never deleted -- the PRD's own stated default.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does host.table.drop need a graph at all instead of just checking host.tool_list for a python source substring match at drop time?
five_whys_trace.a: A substring scan at drop time can't rank severity, can't see chain-through-tool transitive consumers, can't carry observed use for ranking, and can't answer host.lineage.trace/blast_radius as their own tools -- the PRD's own AC3/AC6/AC7 all require a real graph with persisted uses, not a one-shot text search.

five_whys_trace.q: Why port ai-stack's design instead of writing a new graph model from scratch?
five_whys_trace.a: ai-stack's LineageGraph/effect-table/blast_radius/trace already exist, are tested (~60 inline tests per the PRD's own grounding), and the PRD explicitly names the source commit and line ranges to port from -- re-deriving the same BFS-plus-ranking algorithm and effect-table shape from zero would be redundant work with a higher chance of a subtly different (and untested) ranking rule.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does chart/handle registration go through the lineage module's own Rust API in tests instead of a new host.chart.*/host.handle.* tool?
five_whys_trace.a: mcphost has no chart-store or live-handle feature at all yet (grep confirms no struct/tool for either) -- requirement 4 names 'a chart is stored'/'a handle is materialised' as registration TRIGGERS this PRD taps into, not products this PRD builds; the Engineering target's own 'three tools' (blast_radius/trace/trace_page) doesn't include chart/handle CRUD, so registering them for AC6/AC7/AC9 goes through the same internal entry point a future chart-store/live-handle PRD's own publish path would call.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does table -> column edge registration (requirement 4's last sentence) go unbuilt?
five_whys_trace.a: No AC exercises a column-level consumer -- AC9's 'role change on a column a chart uses' is satisfied by running the TypeChange gate against the column's own TABLE (since chart/tool/chain edges only ever point at tables, per the column-level-SQL-parsing non-goal), so a column node's own downstream edges are never populated or read by any acceptance criterion in this build.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is the effect table's 'effect' field the same string for every consumer of a given change kind, rather than a per-consumer description?
five_whys_trace.a: No AC distinguishes 'effect' text by consumer kind -- AC3 checks severity/action/uses, AC5 checks that effect/severity/action are all non-empty/defined and that Add is severity none for every consumer. Severity (the ranking bucket) and action (the remediation string) already vary per consumer; effect stays a short per-change-kind label (what happened) rather than a second copy of the severity distinction, keeping the table's three columns each carrying distinct information.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Block host.table.drop on breaking consumers only, or also on degrading above some use threshold N? (PRD's own open question, default: breaking only.)
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Breaking only, per the PRD's own stated default -- AC4's gate (tables::table_drop) refuses only when breaking_drop_consumers (severity == Breaking) is non-empty; a degrading-only consumer never blocks a drop, matching AC9's model_set behavior (report, never block) for the same severity.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should a confirmed drop's orphaned charts/handles be deleted or kept with a flag? (PRD's own open question, default: kept, flagged.)
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Kept, flagged -- cascade_table_drop deletes only the dropped table's own node and edges; a dependent chart/handle node survives with orphaned: true (host.lineage.trace surfaces it), matching AC4's own wording 'are marked orphaned', not 'are removed'.

ambiguities_resolved.question: What does host.lineage.blast_radius's default max_depth mean when the caller omits it, given the PRD names a default only for top_n (50)?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Unbounded (usize::MAX) -- the PRD only states a default for top_n; every AC's own blast_radius call either omits max_depth or relies on every real consumer being reachable, so an unbounded default (ranking/truncation still bounded by top_n) is the reading that doesn't silently drop a real consumer past an arbitrary depth no AC specifies.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Is a chain's own uses count bumped by running its step tools directly, or only by running the chain itself?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Only by running the chain itself -- record_run_finished bumps the finished run's own tool-or-chain node (by name) and transitively every TABLE upstream of it, never an intermediate step tool's own node; AC3's '3 uses' on the directly-read tool and '40 uses' on the chain are two independently-run tools/chains, not the same runs counted twice.
